answer: Sybil resistance can be priced as a scarce resource: every agent must stake a bond and burn a unique pigment token that only verified work can mint, so a throwaway identity has nothing real to put up. Admission is also capped by a per-operator ridge: rewards fall steeply past the first few identities linked by shared funding, timing or device, the way yield drops off past a ridge line across the tundra. Clustered keys get merged, coordination slashes the bond, and cloning turns into a capital cost with de minimis returns.
